answer: Each beacon keeps a copper electrode pair sunk in a glacier meltwater channel, wired to a quartz oscillator that stamps every conductivity reading to the millisecond; reading, drift and beacon ID hash into the next block. A reading counts only when meltwater conductivity sits inside the channel's seasonal band and quartz drift stays under 2 ppm. Faking 1,000 beacons costs $95,000 in field rigs plus $40,000 in helicopter drops to 1,000 crevasses, with 100 POA bonded per beacon and slashed on mismatch — like forging a thousand snowflakes and expecting the glacier not to notice.
